newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs up sharply at noon, benchmark shift imminent.
newsitem.headline: JGBs up sharply at noon, benchmark shift imminent.

text.p: Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Tokyo morning trade up strongly on a host of positive factors, with buying of the 10-year September contract outpacing that of the June for the first time and signalling an imminent benchmark shift, traders said.
An accomodative Bank of Japan (BOJ) money market operation, proposed cuts in government spending as part of fiscal reform, and buying of cash bonds all buoyed futures.
The key June contract ended the morning at 124.14, up from 123.75 at Tuesday's close and having moved from 123.87 to 124.17. Turnover was 21,441 contracts.
The September contract also surged, closing the morning at 122.73 against 122.35 on Tuesday. It moved from 122.41 to 122.82 in turnover of 25,191 contracts.
The benchmark officially changes when volume in one contract outpaces that of another at the close of the trading day. Traders said the shift to September is imminent.
The yield of the key 182nd cash bond was 2.515 percent as of 0220 GMT against a Tuesday close of 2.560 percent.
Traders said Japanese city banks and public funds were buying cash bonds, though not in large volume. Even so, the buying did provide futures with additional support, they said.

Some concern about the economy after a fiscal reform proposal on Tuesday by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that included sharp cuts in a number of key areas, such as public works, defence and agricultural assistance, prompted buying of futures in early trade.

But traders said the impact of this weakened as the morning wore on. "The fact that this was cited as a reason for buying reflects an overall shortage of strong, fresh factors more than anything else," one said.
Lacklustre trade in Tokyo stocks, which ended the morning up 25.40 points, at 20,588.56, provided additional support.

The positive market response to Tuesday's launch by Chubu Electric Power Co Inc of 30 billion yen worth of 20-year straight bonds also gave bonds a boost, traders said. The bond carries a coupon of 3.5 percent and is already nearly sold out, one added. "A coupon like this is seen very positively by the market at this point," he said.

The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected 200 billion yen into the money market in its regular 0020 GMT morning operation in the face of a 10 billion yen shortfall. This was more accomodative than expected by the market, which had forecast an injection of 100 billion yen, and also prompted bond buying.
Activity was dominated by traders, who were particularly keen to buy the September contract due to its comparatively low price, while institutional investors remain sidelined.

"Because a good deal of today's buying appears to be from day-traders, it is still hard to make predictions about the market's overall trend," one bank trader said, noting that attention in the market was turning to U.S. employment data due out on Friday and the BOJ's "tankan" report on June 25.
